title: Regulating longevity-medicine clinics
asked: Ms Joan Pereira asked what regulatory and enforcement measures ensure longevity-medicine clinics follow safe medical practices and science-based, evidence-based treatments to protect clients and patients.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said all outpatient medical service providers, including longevity-medicine services, must be licensed under the Healthcare Services Act and comply with it. Medical practitioners must follow the Singapore Medical Council's Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines, which require safe, rational and evidence-based treatments. Non-standard treatments should only be given in a clinical study with prior Institutional Research Board approval. Services are monitored through inspections and audits, and providers that fail standards may face regulatory action including imprisonment and financial penalties; the Ministry can lodge a complaint with the SMC.

key_points.point: All outpatient medical service providers, including longevity-medicine services, must be licensed under the Healthcare Services Act.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: must be licensed and comply with the requirements under the Healthcare Services Act (HCSA)

key_points.point: Medical practitioners must adhere to the Singapore Medical Council's Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: medical practitioners are required to adhere to the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (ECEG)

key_points.point: Both the HCSA and SMC guidelines require safe, rational and evidence-based medical treatments in line with accepted clinical practice.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: require medical service providers and practitioners to provide only safe, rational and evidence-based medical treatments in accordance with accepted clinical practice

key_points.point: Non-standard medical treatments should only be provided in the context of a clinical study.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Where non-standard medical treatments are considered, they should only be provided in the context of a clinical study

key_points.point: Such clinical studies must comply with ethical requirements, including prior approval from a local Institutional Research Board.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Such studies must comply with the ethical requirements for research studies including prior approval from a local Institutional Research Board

key_points.point: Services are monitored through routine inspections and compliance audits, which may also be triggered by complaints.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: These services are monitored through routine inspections and compliance audits, which may also be triggered by complaints

key_points.point: Providers that fail to meet standards may face regulatory action or enforcement measures including imprisonment and financial penalties.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon

key_points.point: If the Ministry receives information that a practitioner has not followed the SMC guidelines, it will lodge a complaint with the SMC.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the Ministry will lodge a complaint against the medical practitioner to the SMC

key_points.point: The public is encouraged to discuss appropriate and evidence-based tests and treatments with their doctor.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The public is encouraged to discuss with their doctor on appropriate and evidence-based tests and treatments recommended in their individual circumstances

key_points.point: For the general population, healthy lifestyle habits remain foundational to maintaining good health.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: adopting healthy lifestyle habits such as a balanced diet, adequate sleep, regular exercise and staying socially engaged remains foundational to maintaining good health
